entities.name: absorption spectrum
entities.definition: An absorption spectrum represents a specific pattern where dark lines appear superimposed upon an otherwise continuous background of light. This phenomenon occurs because atoms within a cooler gas absorb photons at precise wavelengths, removing them from the transmitted beam and revealing unique elemental fingerprints.

entities.name: aurora
entities.definition: An aurora represents light radiated by atoms and ions within the ionosphere when excited by charged particles arriving from the Sun. This phenomenon is predominantly observed in magnetic polar regions due to the specific interaction between solar wind and Earth's magnetospheric fields.

entities.name: Doppler effect
entities.definition: The Doppler effect describes the shift in radiation frequency caused by relative motion between source and observer. When an object moves away, wavelengths stretch to redshift; approaching objects compress waves into blueshift, allowing astronomers to measure stellar velocities.

entities.name: simple harmonic motion
entities.definition: Simple harmonic motion describes oscillatory movement in systems where net force follows Hooke's law. This specific type of periodic motion occurs when restoring forces are directly proportional to displacement from equilibrium.

examples: A mass on an ideal spring oscillates with constant period.
A small-angle pendulum approximates simple harmonic motion.

formal.statement: Simple harmonic motion is periodic motion whose acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward the equilibrium position.

applications: Tuning guitar strings for specific musical note frequencies.
Designing building dampers to reduce earthquake structural sway.
Analyzing pendulum clocks for precise timekeeping mechanisms.
limitations: Assumes ideal springs with zero internal friction or damping.

Requires strictly linear restoring forces proportional to displacement.
